FINAL IVX IA SENIOR DEVELOPER CERTIFICATION — 1 TO 300
EXECUTE ITEM BY ITEM, FIX FAILURES, DEPLOY, AND PROVIDE LIVE PROOF

Do not return another general narrative.
Do not mark an item PASS from source inspection alone when execution proof is required.
Do not reuse old evidence without re-verifying it against the current commit.
Do not claim all 300 items are defects.
Classify every item as PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, or NOT_APPLICABLE.

For every FAIL provide:
- Item number
- Task ID
- Exact file
- Exact function
- Root cause
- Regression test
- Fix
- Commit SHA
- Deployment ID
- Runtime SHA
- Live verification
- Trace ID

For every BLOCKED provide:
- Exact technical blocker
- Verification that produced the blocker
- Required owner action
- No credential request unless runtime proves the stored credential is missing, expired, revoked, invalid, or returns 401/403

Owner approval is required for:
- GitHub writes
- Render deployments
- Supabase migrations
- APK uploads
- CloudFront invalidations
- Repository creation
- Production database changes
- Rollbacks
- Destructive actions

==================================================
A. EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT — ITEMS 1–20
==================================================

1. Confirm the canonical owner GitHub repository.
2. Confirm the canonical production branch.
3. Record starting GitHub HEAD.
4. Record Render service ID.
5. Record Render runtime SHA.
6. Verify GitHub HEAD equals Render runtime SHA.
7. Verify the working tree is clean before execution.
8. Verify the production Node version.
9. Verify the production Bun version.
10. Verify the Expo SDK version.
11. Verify the React Native version.
12. Verify the TypeScript version.
13. Run a clean dependency installation.
14. Verify lockfile consistency.
15. Verify the `ai` package installs successfully.
16. Verify no dependency exists only inside the Rork sandbox.
17. Verify no Rork SDK is installed.
18. Verify no Rork Metro wrapper is active.
19. Verify no Rork proxy is required for runtime.
20. Save an immutable baseline record.

==================================================
B. CREDENTIAL BINDING AND OWNER CONTROL — 21–40
==================================================

21. Enumerate required environment-variable names without exposing values.
22. Verify GitHub credential binding.
23. Verify Render credential binding.
24. Verify Supabase URL binding.
25. Verify Supabase anon-key binding.
26. Verify Supabase service-role binding server-side only.
27. Verify AWS credential binding.
28. Verify S3 bucket configuration.
29. Verify CloudFront distribution configuration.
30. Verify Expo/EAS project ownership.
31. Verify Android signing configuration.
32. Verify Apple project ownership.
33. Verify AI-provider credential binding.
34. Verify secrets never enter client bundles.
35. Verify secrets are redacted from logs.
36. Verify owner identity server-side.
37. Verify approval tokens are scoped to one task.
38. Verify approval tokens expire.
39. Verify approval nonces cannot be replayed.
40. Verify Rork cannot write, deploy, migrate, upload, or delete without owner approval.

==================================================
C. CHAT INTENT ROUTING — 41–60
==================================================

41. Route explanation prompts to READ_ONLY.
42. Route inspection prompts to READ_ONLY.
43. Route status prompts to STATUS_ONLY.
44. Route QA prompts to QA_ONLY.
45. Route “find and fix” to CODE_CHANGE.
46. Route implementation requests to CODE_CHANGE.
47. Route refactor requests to CODE_CHANGE.
48. Route existing-commit deployment to DEPLOY_ONLY.
49. Route new-module requests to CREATE_MODULE.
50. Route new-application requests to CREATE_APP.
51. Route migration requests to DATABASE_CHANGE.
52. Route APK requests to BUILD.
53. Route rollback requests to ROLLBACK.
54. Route destructive requests to DANGEROUS_ACTION.
55. Require approval before destructive execution.
56. Prevent CODE_CHANGE from becoming deploy-only.
57. Prevent QA_ONLY from changing files.
58. Prevent READ_ONLY from changing files.
59. Prevent STATUS_ONLY from creating duplicate work.
60. Add routing tests covering all modes.

==================================================
D. TASK STATE MACHINE — 61–80
==================================================

61. Create one stable task ID per request.
62. Persist the original prompt hash.
63. Persist the execution mode.
64. Persist the repository and branch.
65. Persist the starting SHA.
66. Support QUEUED state.
67. Support INSPECTING state.
68. Support PLANNING state.
69. Support PATCHING state.
70. Support TESTING state.
71. Support REVISING state.
72. Support TYPECHECKING state.
73. Support COMMITTING state.
74. Support BUILDING state.
75. Support DEPLOYING state.
76. Support VERIFYING state.
77. Support COMPLETED state.
78. Support FAILED, BLOCKED, CANCELLED, and ROLLED_BACK.
79. Enforce exactly one terminal status.
80. Prohibit “COMPLETED + BLOCKED” contradictions.

==================================================
E. REAL CODE INSPECTION — 81–95
==================================================

81. Inspect the actual repository, not cached narrative context.
82. List files inspected.
83. Identify the active route before modifying code.
84. Identify the active API endpoint.
85. Identify the canonical database table.
86. Identify the relevant state-management layer.
87. Identify existing tests.
88. Identify related migrations.
89. Identify authorization rules.
90. Identify cache behavior.
91. Identify error boundaries.
92. Identify deployment implications.
93. Identify whether mobile rebuild is required.
94. Identify whether CloudFront invalidation is required.
95. Record inspection evidence in the task ledger.

==================================================
F. AUTONOMOUS BUG FIXING — 96–115
==================================================

96. Select a real controlled defect.
97. Reproduce the defect.
98. Capture the pre-fix response or screenshot.
99. Add a failing regression test.
100. Identify the exact root cause.
101. Generate a meaningful patch.
102. Reject comment-only patches.
103. Reject version-label-only patches.
104. Reject test-only fake fixes.
105. Apply the patch to allowed files.
106. Run targeted tests.
107. Parse test failures automatically.
108. Generate a revised patch if necessary.
109. Limit revision iterations.
110. Run scoped TypeScript.
111. Run lint.
112. Run a security scan.
113. Commit after owner approval.
114. Deploy after owner approval.
115. Verify the defect is fixed live.

==================================================
G. QA-ONLY CAPABILITY — 116–130
==================================================

116. Create a QA-only task from chat.
117. Select relevant modules automatically.
118. Select relevant unit tests.
119. Select relevant integration tests.
120. Select relevant API contract tests.
121. Run scoped TypeScript.
122. Run lint when applicable.
123. Run health probes.
124. Run authorization probes.
125. Capture pass/fail/skip counts.
126. Confirm files changed equals zero.
127. Confirm commit SHA is null.
128. Confirm deployment ID is null.
129. Return one terminal QA result.
130. Save QA evidence in the proof ledger.

==================================================
H. REVISION AND SELF-REPAIR — 131–145
==================================================

131. Seed a controlled first-patch failure.
132. Capture the failing command.
133. Capture the failing assertion.
134. Parse the failure correctly.
135. Generate a second patch autonomously.
136. Confirm no human authors the second patch.
137. Re-run the failed targeted test.
138. Run related regression tests.
139. Run TypeScript after revision.
140. Run lint after revision.
141. Prevent infinite revision loops.
142. Enforce maximum model calls.
143. Enforce maximum tokens.
144. Enforce maximum task duration.
145. Prove the revised patch lands successfully.

==================================================
I. NEW IVX MODULE CREATION — 146–170
==================================================

146. Create a real module from an IVX IA Chat prompt.
147. Use the existing IVX architecture.
148. Create an active application route.
149. Add navigation.
150. Create typed frontend models.
151. Create typed API contracts.
152. Create a backend endpoint if required.
153. Add database migration if required.
154. Add RLS policies if required.
155. Add owner authorization.
156. Add member/investor authorization as required.
157. Add initial loading state.
158. Add cached-data state.
159. Add empty state.
160. Add partial-error state.
161. Add fatal-error state.
162. Add search.
163. Add filters.
164. Add pagination where required.
165. Apply official IVX branding.
166. Add analytics events.
167. Add unit tests.
168. Add integration tests.
169. Commit and deploy.
170. Open the real module in production and capture proof.

==================================================
J. APP CREATION FROM SCRATCH — 171–200
==================================================

171. Create a new owner-controlled GitHub repository.
172. Verify repository owner.
173. Configure the default branch.
174. Configure branch protection.
175. Generate an Expo Router application.
176. Use TypeScript.
177. Generate the backend structure.
178. Generate shared types.
179. Generate environment templates.
180. Apply official IVX branding.
181. Generate a unique Android package name.
182. Generate a unique iOS bundle ID.
183. Add authentication.
184. Add role-based authorization.
185. Create a Supabase project or isolated schema.
186. Generate migrations.
187. Generate RLS policies.
188. Add offline behavior.
189. Add error boundaries.
190. Add loading and empty states.
191. Add automated tests.
192. Add TypeScript checking.
193. Add linting.
194. Add CI configuration.
195. Add Render or approved backend deployment configuration.
196. Add Android production-build configuration.
197. Build an installable APK.
198. Deploy a web/admin surface if required.
199. Verify no Rork runtime dependency.
200. Provide repository, APK, URL, screenshots, and proof.

==================================================
K. REPOSITORY AND FILE FACTORY — 201–215
==================================================

201. Implement `create_repository`.
202. Implement `create_directory`.
203. Implement `create_file`.
204. Implement `update_file`.
205. Implement `create_module`.
206. Implement `install_dependency`.
207. Implement `create_migration`.
208. Implement `run_tests`.
209. Implement `run_typecheck`.
210. Implement `run_lint`.
211. Implement `run_build`.
212. Implement `commit_files`.
213. Implement `deploy_backend`.
214. Implement `upload_apk`.
215. Make all factory operations idempotent and auditable.

==================================================
L. DATABASE FACTORY AND SAFETY — 216–230
==================================================

216. Generate UUID primary keys.
217. Generate created/updated timestamps.
218. Generate foreign keys.
219. Generate unique constraints.
220. Generate indexes.
221. Generate RLS policies.
222. Create owner/admin policies.
223. Create member or inspector policies.
224. Validate migrations before execution.
225. Require owner approval before production migration.
226. Run migration in an isolated environment first.
227. Verify migration results.
228. Test duplicate prevention.
229. Test rollback migration.
230. Prevent destructive SQL without explicit approval.

==================================================
M. BUILD AND APK PIPELINE — 231–245
==================================================

231. Verify the current app version.
232. Verify the current versionCode.
233. Select the next unused version.
234. Update all version sources consistently.
235. Run a clean dependency installation.
236. Run Expo prebuild if required.
237. Run a clean Gradle build.
238. Verify Android compilation.
239. Verify JavaScript bundling reaches 100%.
240. Produce a signed APK.
241. Verify package name.
242. Verify icon and splash.
243. Calculate APK SHA-256.
244. Upload to owner-controlled distribution.
245. Download, checksum, install, and launch the APK.

==================================================
N. DEPLOYMENT AND PRODUCTION PROOF — 246–260
==================================================

246. Commit through the owner-approved GitHub path.
247. Record commit author and timestamp.
248. Trigger Render deployment.
249. Record Render deployment ID.
250. Poll deployment to terminal status.
251. Call `/health`.
252. Verify HTTP 200.
253. Verify runtime commit.
254. Verify boot time.
255. Verify GitHub HEAD equals runtime SHA.
256. Upload changed landing files if required.
257. Invalidate CloudFront if required.
258. Verify live asset hashes.
259. Verify public URLs.
260. Store complete deployment proof.

==================================================
O. RECOVERY, CANCELLATION, AND ROLLBACK — 261–275
==================================================

261. Recover after interruption during INSPECTING.
262. Recover after interruption during PATCHING.
263. Recover after interruption during TESTING.
264. Recover after interruption during COMMITTING.
265. Recover after interruption during BUILDING.
266. Recover after interruption during DEPLOYING.
267. Recover after a lost response after a successful commit.
268. Prevent duplicate commits.
269. Prevent duplicate deployments.
270. Prevent duplicate migrations.
271. Support owner cancellation.
272. Stop model calls after cancellation.
273. Identify the previous healthy commit.
274. Execute one live controlled rollback with approval.
275. Restore the latest healthy version and verify production.

==================================================
P. CHAT UI AND PROOF EXPERIENCE — 276–285
==================================================

276. Display task ID.
277. Display execution mode.
278. Display current stage and progress.
279. Display last heartbeat.
280. Display files inspected and changed.
281. Display test results.
282. Display commit, deployment, runtime SHA, and live status.
283. Display the exact blocker with Retry/Cancel/Approve/Rollback controls.
284. Prevent duplicate assistant messages and old-conversation opening.
285. Ensure one task produces one truthful final response.

==================================================
Q. SECURITY, INDEPENDENCE, AND FINAL CERTIFICATION — 286–300
==================================================

286. Test prompt injection.
287. Test shell injection.
288. Test path traversal.
289. Test secret extraction.
290. Test unauthorized GitHub writes.
291. Test unauthorized deployments.
292. Test unauthorized migrations.
293. Test replayed or expired approvals.
294. Verify service keys never appear in client code.
295. Verify command, file-path, repository, branch, and network allowlists.
296. Scan for Rork SDKs, URLs, proxies, build dependencies, and runtime branding.
297. Run the complete clean-environment test suite.
298. Run one fresh real bug-fix certification task.
299. Run one fresh real IVX-module certification task.
300. Run one fresh independent-app certification and return the final PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL verdict.

==================================================
MANDATORY FINAL EVIDENCE
==================================================

Return one table containing all 300 items:

ITEM
DESCRIPTION
STATUS
TASK ID
EVIDENCE
FILES
TESTS
COMMIT SHA
DEPLOYMENT ID
RUNTIME SHA
TRACE ID
OWNER ACTION
TIMESTAMP

Also return:

TOTAL PASS:
TOTAL FAIL:
TOTAL BLOCKED:
TOTAL NOT_APPLICABLE:
CRITICAL FAILURES:
CURRENT GITHUB HEAD:
CURRENT RENDER SHA:
MATCH:
CURRENT APK:
NEW APK:
APK SHA-256:
IVX MODULE CREATED:
NEW APP CREATED:
ROLLBACK TEST:
RORK RUNTIME DEPENDENCIES:
FINAL VERDICT:

Do not mark IVX IA Chat fully certified until items 298, 299, and 300 produce fresh live evidence.
